read_notes: MUST use encoding='utf-8-sig': the file starts with a UTF-8 BOM and the first header cell is EMPTY, so without the BOM strip the first column name becomes '\ufeff'. Line terminator is CRLF; pandas' C engine handles it. dtype=str + keep_default_na=False + na_values=[''] is required to (a) stop pandas coercing pincode/SrNo/lat/lon to float and printing them in scientific notation, (b) stop it turning the literal strings 'NA'/'null' into NaN, and (c) preserve leading zeros. Do NOT use index_col=0 - the first column is a stale pandas index with 106 gaps and is not a usable key.
row_count_explanation: wc -l reports 10612 physical lines. csv.reader returns 10531 records (10530 data + 1 header): the gap of 81 is caused by 81 cells containing an embedded CRLF inside a quoted field (all of them in District_Name / Taluka_Name, value 'Almora\\\n' and one 'Chilakaluripet\\\n H/O.Purushotha Patnam Mandal'). Of those 10530 parsed rows, 203 are completely empty in all 24 data columns and carry only a stale pandas index in column 1 - 200 form a contiguous trailing block (positions 10330-10529) and 3 are interior (positions 4789, 5740, 6444). TRUE LOGICAL ROW COUNT = 10327. (10612 - 81 embedded newlines - 1 header - 203 empty = 10327.)

columns.name: Unnamed: 0

It is a pandas RangeIndex written out by a previous `df.to_csv()`: strictly increasing 0..10635, unique, but with 106 gaps -> 106 rows were deleted after that export. Carries no facility information. Keep only as `source_row_order` provenance if desired.

columns.name: SrNo
columns.notes: Unique across all 10327 real rows, integer 1..192898 -> this file is a ~5.4% subset of a much larger parent register keyed by the same SrNo. Not file-ordered (not monotonic). Best available source PK; also the join key back to the parent system.

columns.name: Health Facility Name

columns.notes: 60.00% filled. 34 '0', 27 '-', 23 '\N'. Mixed formats (with/without STD code, hyphenated, comma-separated multiples in 141 rows). 832 values (13.4%) are 10-digit numbers starting 6-9, i.e. personal MOBILE numbers, and 2 cells contain an email address instead of a number. columns.name: latitude
columns.notes: 97.83% non-null on real rows; all non-null values parse as float. 68 are exactly 0. Decimal precision varies 0-9 places (75 values have no decimal part).

columns.name: longitude
columns.notes: 97.83% non-null; 69 exactly 0; min -115.20 and max 118.66 confirm out-of-India junk exists.

columns.name: altitude
columns.notes: REAL values, not junk - but 62.20% are the sentinel 0 and 23 are '\N', leaving only 3881 rows (37.6%) with a real elevation. Non-zero range 0.26-5985 m, median 175 m, and the state-level medians are geographically correct (J&K 1589 m, Uttarakhand 1320 m, Meghalaya 1019 m, Delhi ~0). Fill is source-batch dependent (97.9% non-zero in Tamil Nadu, 0.16% in Delhi, 0% in Chandigarh/Goa/Tripura/Puducherry) so 0 means 'not captured', not 'sea level'. A handful are wrong (three Auraiya UP facilities carry 2700 m; the true elevation there is ~130 m).

'Others' (2382 rows, 23%) is mostly private hospitals/nursing homes.

Stripping the prefix raises the name+district near-dupe count from 176 to 239 (+63). Proof it conceals real duplicates: SrNo 89661 'Gingla CHC' (Udaipur, latitude=0) carries Notes='Duplicate or SR No. 85112', and SrNo 85112 is in this file as 'NOTIONAL Gingla CHC', same district, valid geo. Strip the prefix into a separate flag before any name matching.

duplicates.method: exact = duplicated() on all 24 data columns. exact_ignoring_srno excludes SrNo and 'Non filled numbering'. near_dupe_name_geo = duplicated() on lowercased/punct-stripped facility name + lat/lon rounded to 3 decimals, restricted to the 10106 rows with geo inside the India bbox. near_dupe_name_district = same normalized name + raw District_Name over all rows. Counts are EXTRA rows (keep='first'); *_groups counts are total rows involved.

geo_quality.partition_note: The five buckets are mutually exclusive and sum to n_rows.

candidate_primary_key.note: Unique and 100% populated on all 10327 real rows. Range 1..192898 means this file is a ~5.4% extract of a much larger parent register that uses the same numbering. Recommended source PK: NIN:<SrNo>. The first column (BOM-only header) is also unique but is a stale pandas index with 106 gaps - do not use it.

auto_vs_manual_pairs.recommendation: COALESCE(manual, auto) for all three pairs. The manual column is the later human-verified value: it is only ever populated on rows a coder worked, and on those rows the auto value is frequently a sentinel ('0', '\N') or a bare town word. It is never populated where the auto value is absent-and-good. Keep both, expose the auto value as *_raw for audit.

curation_workflow.note: 'Non filled numbering' and 'Manual Health Facility Name' have identical non-null masks (623 rows). Coder is filled on 600 rows and Manually_added on 526, so the three markers are not co-extensive; 628 rows carry at least one curation marker (6.08%). Coder='tanmay' has 73 rows with a blank Manually_added - Coder is the more reliable 'a human touched this row' flag.
curation_workflow.coder_pii_assessment: YES - PII, low sensitivity. The values are the first names of 5 identifiable internal staff (tanmay, shalmali, mallika, sweta, sid) with no contact detail attached. It is employee-attribution metadata, not facility data. Retain it in the internal provenance table for audit/quality attribution; exclude it from any user-facing or LLM-queryable view, or replace with an opaque coder_id.

sentinels.note: '\N' is the MySQL/mysqldump NULL marker, so this CSV was produced by an SQL export, not by Excel.

er_readiness.note: (name, district, geo) is fully viable: 97.80% of rows carry all three and only 6 rows (0.06%) lack a usable name-or-district. The real risk is not missing data but AMBIGUOUS names - 43.24% of names contain no facility-type keyword and are bare place names, and 1293 rows sit on a coordinate shared with a different facility (block-centroid geocoding), so geo alone must not be used to confirm a match at tighter than ~1 km.
